messages:
maya: heads-up — onboarding a HF chat model (gpt-ish-7b) and noticed system role text gets duplicated then dropped after conversion to generation_config.json
jordan: ugh, hmm. any chance it’s tokenization differences for the special sys/sep tokens?
liam: can you paste the HF `chat_template` and the resulting Redwood generation params? small snippets ok
maya: sure — HF template we ship: ```json
{"system":"You are a helpful assistant.","user":"{input}","assistant":""}
```
maya: and generation_config.json produced by the HF->Redwood script ended up with: ```json
{"temperature":1.0,"top_p":0.95,"top_k":50,"repetition_penalty":1.0,"special_tokens":{"system":"","assistant":"","sep":"<|endoftext|>"}}
```
maya: note `system` became empty string which explains duplication when client reconstructs the prompt
jordan: ah — the converter treats unknown special token values as literal empty token. HF models sometimes use `` or  for system markers and the tokenizer maps them to -1 or None; converter should preserve as-absent not empty-string
liam: repro attempt: if tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids('') -> raises or returns None, our script currently does `str(token)` so None -> ""
liam: quick patch: treat falsy/None as omit-key in the json output instead of empty string.
maya: worked locally! patch avoids empty system token. but still seeing subtle sampling diffs between HF default sampling and Redwood runtime defaults — top_k/top_p behavior looks off for chat templates
jordan: what differences exactly? seed/sample examples?
maya: with same seed and input: HF sampling yields more conservative replies (lower repetition), Redwood default mapping used temp=1.0 top_p=0.95 top_k=50 rp=1.0 but HF model config had top_k=0(top-k disabled) and top_p=0.92 and rp=1.1
maya: converter should prefer explicit HF values over Redwood fallback mapping. Right now fallback map applies before reading hf config if model metadata missing
liam: agreed. plan: conversion priority = model.generation_config > tokenizer.special_tokens_map > global-defaults. also treat top_k=0 as disabled (set to null in Redwood)
jordan: add unit test: sample deterministic prompt + quantized runtime with same tokens to assert n-gram repetition score and a small KL over token distributions. Also add regression test for special token preservation.
maya: adding tests now. one edge-case: HF uses `pad_token` for chat delim sometimes; if pad==eos we must not drop eos mapping else we lose sentence termination during batching
liam: good catch. I'll add conversion rule: if pad_token_id == eos_token_id -> keep pad_token name but set behavior to be treated as eos in runtime (flag pad_is_eos=true)
maya: thanks. deploy-bot: rolling patch to staging branch -> #2345
deploy-bot: deploy started for branch genconv/special-token-fix, build 3824
eval-bot: running comparison evals (deterministic samples + 100 chats) against reference HF outputs, will post metrics in #model-evals when done
jordan: sweet. follow-up action: update docs snippet for generation_config mapping and add note about top_k=0 semantics and pad==eos caveat
maya: will do. if eval-bot shows regressions we'll iterate. :thumbsup:
